title: Inside the mind of an octopus, with Jennifer Mather, PhD

sentences.en: It's no surprise that we Homo sapiens tend to have a human-centric view of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我们智人倾向于以人类为中心来看待智慧，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: When we think of smart animals, we generally think of primates or other animals close to us on the evolutionary tree.
sentences.zh: 当我们想到聪明的动物时，通常会想到灵长类动物或其他在进化树上与我们相近的动物。

sentences.en: But octopuses shake up this view of the world.
sentences.zh: 但章鱼打破了这种世界观。

sentences.en: They haven't shared a common ancestor with humans in at least 600 million years.
sentences.zh: 它们与人类至少有6亿年没有共同祖先了。

sentences.en: But somehow, these invertebrates evolved remarkable problem-solving abilities, curiosity, and an intelligence all their own.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，这些无脊椎动物进化出了非凡的解决问题的能力、好奇心以及它们独有的智慧。

sentences.en: So what do we know about how octopuses think and how they experience the world?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们对章鱼的思维方式及其感知世界的方式了解多少呢？

sentences.en: How and why did they evolve to be so curious and smart?
sentences.zh: 它们是如何以及为什么进化得如此好奇和聪明的？

sentences.en: How are their brains structured?
sentences.zh: 它们的大脑结构是怎样的？

sentences.en: And what can we learn about thinking and intelligence in general from studying how octopuses behave?
sentences.zh: 通过研究章鱼的行为，我们能对一般的思维和智慧学到什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，

sentences.en: Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Jennifer
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是詹妮弗·马瑟博士，

sentences.en: Mather, a professor of psychology at the University of Lethbridge in Alberta, Canada, and one of the world's leading experts on octopus behavior.
sentences.zh: 她是加拿大阿尔伯塔省莱斯布里奇大学的心理学教授，也是全球领先的章鱼行为专家之一。

sentences.en: Dr. Mather has spent decades studying cephalopods, marine animals that include octopuses, cuttlefish, and squids.
sentences.zh: 马瑟博士花了数十年时间研究头足类动物，这类海洋动物包括章鱼、乌贼和鱿鱼。

sentences.en: Her fieldwork has taken her around the world to places including Bermuda, Hawaii, Bonaire, and the Pacific Island, Moria.
sentences.zh: 她的实地考察足迹遍布全球，包括百慕大、夏威夷、博内尔岛和太平洋岛屿莫雷阿岛。

sentences.en: She's authored dozens of academic papers and is co-author of the book Octopus, the Ocean's Intelligent Invertebrate.
sentences.zh: 她撰写了数十篇学术论文，并合著了《章鱼：海洋中聪明的无脊椎动物》一书。

sentences.en: She was also the scientific advisor to the Netflix film My Octopus Teacher, which won the 2021 Academy Award for
sentences.zh: 她还是Netflix电影《我的章鱼老师》的科学顾问，该片获得了2021年奥斯卡

sentences.en: Best Documentary.
sentences.zh: 最佳纪录片奖。

sentences.en: And if you haven't watched it, you really should.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没看过，真的应该去看一看。

sentences.en: Dr. Mather, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 马瑟博士，感谢您今天参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: And I mentioned in the introduction that octopuses are very far removed from us on the evolutionary tree.
sentences.zh: 我在介绍中提到，章鱼在进化树上与我们相距甚远。

sentences.en: So far removed that some people compare meeting an octopus to meeting an alien life form.
sentences.zh: 远到有些人将遇见章鱼比作遇见外星生命。

sentences.en: What do you think of that analogy?
sentences.zh: 您如何看待这个类比？

sentences.en: Oh, I'm not really happy about that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不太喜欢这个说法。

sentences.en: Let's say that life on this planet is very, very diverse.
sentences.zh: 我们得说，这个星球上的生命是非常、非常多样化的。

sentences.en: So octopuses are completely not like us.
sentences.zh: 所以章鱼完全不像我们。

sentences.en: On the other hand, honeybees are completely not like us.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，蜜蜂也完全不像我们。

sentences.en: And they're not like octopuses either.
sentences.zh: 而且它们也不像章鱼。

sentences.en: So octopuses give us a glimpse into diversity.
sentences.zh: 所以章鱼让我们得以一窥生命的多样性。

sentences.en: Why do you believe that octopuses evolved to be so intelligent?
sentences.zh: 您为什么认为章鱼进化得如此聪明？

sentences.en: What were the evolutionary pressures at work?
sentences.zh: 当时有哪些进化压力在起作用？

sentences.en: Probably the evolutionary pressures were the competition of the bony fishes.
sentences.zh: 进化压力可能来自于硬骨鱼类的竞争。

sentences.en: Because the bony fishes evolved about the time that the colioid cephalopods evolved.
sentences.zh: 因为硬骨鱼类大约是在鞘形亚纲头足类动物进化时出现的。

sentences.en: And bony fishes really now dominate the ocean.
sentences.zh: 而硬骨鱼类现在确实统治着海洋。

sentences.en: They're fast, they're smart, they're maneuverable.
sentences.zh: 它们速度快、聪明、机动性强。

sentences.en: And to keep up with them, the cephalopods had to evolve, if not necessarily to be fast, maybe to be smart.
sentences.zh: 为了跟上它们，头足类动物不得不进化，即使不一定非要变快，也许得变聪明。

sentences.en: Do you have any salient examples of behavior that show how smart or curious octopuses are?
sentences.zh: 您有什么显著的行为例子能展示章鱼有多聪明或多好奇吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what can they do that might surprise people?
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们能做什么让人惊讶的事情？

sentences.en: But one of the things that everybody quotes is what they call the coconut carrying octopuses in Australia.
sentences.zh: 大家经常引用的一个例子是澳大利亚的“椰子章鱼”。

sentences.en: And a group of octopuses dug out, separated coconut halves from the muddy sand, and wandered off across in the open area, carrying them underneath them.
sentences.zh: 一群章鱼从泥沙中挖出并分开了椰子壳，然后带着它们在开阔区域游走，把椰子壳托在身下。

sentences.en: And after a while, when they got to the point that they wanted to stop and rest, they drop the two halves, separate them, neatly line them up, crawl inside, pull it over
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，当它们想停下来休息时，就会放下两半椰子壳，把它们分开，整齐地排好，爬进去，把它们拉到

sentences.en: between them, I guess you'd call it, and find themselves perfect shelter.
sentences.zh: 自己身上——我想你可以这么说——从而找到了完美的避难所。

sentences.en: That's really interesting because that's something that has been called mental time travel, which is thinking about how the
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣，因为这被称为“心理时间旅行”，也就是思考

sentences.en: world is going to be in the future and making plans for what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 未来世界会是什么样，并为此制定计划。

sentences.en: That's pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: And that reminds me of a scene in My Octopus Teacher, where the octopus that was basically the star of the show, created a kind of armor using old shells and seafloor detritus.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起《我的章鱼老师》里的一个场景，那只作为主角的章鱼用旧贝壳和海底碎屑制造了一种盔甲。

sentences.en: And it appeared to be very deliberate behavior to protect itself from a predator shark.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是一种非常有目的性的行为，为了保护自己免受鲨鱼捕食。

sentences.en: And we often hear that there are very few animals that use tools like we humans do.
sentences.zh: 我们经常听说很少有动物像我们人类一样使用工具。

sentences.en: But does this behavior and the coconut behavior indicate that octopuses are also using tools?
sentences.zh: 但这种行为和椰子行为是否表明章鱼也在使用工具？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: And one of the ways in which it's really clear is that they will hide in some kind of shelter.
sentences.zh: 其中一个非常明显的表现是它们会躲在某种避难所里。

sentences.en: And of course, the shelters have different sizes of entrances as well as different spaces behind.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些避难所的入口大小不同，后面的空间也不同。

sentences.en: And way back when I was studying octopuses in Bermuda, I was trying to figure out how you could characterize their shelters.
sentences.zh: 很久以前我在百慕大研究章鱼时，曾试图找出如何描述它们的避难所。

sentences.en: And one thing I noticed is the bigger the entrance, the more likely the octopus was to bring rocks and shells and pile them up in front of it to make the entrance smaller.
sentences.zh: 我注意到的一件事是，入口越大，章鱼就越有可能搬来岩石和贝壳，堆在入口前把入口变小。

sentences.en: And that's tool use.
sentences.zh: 这就是工具使用。

sentences.en: But actually, my favorite tool use of theirs is they have a flexible siphon or funnel, which is really exhalant, as it would be if we blew out water.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我最喜欢的它们的工具使用方式是，它们有一个灵活的虹吸管或漏斗，这实际上是排泄器官，就像我们呼出水一样。

sentences.en: And they use this water jet for a whole bunch of things.
sentences.zh: 它们利用这个喷水管做很多事情。

sentences.en: They use it to clean out holes.
sentences.zh: 它们用它来清理洞穴。

sentences.en: They use it to repel nuisances, not really big predators, but nuisances, which includes, of course, my roping hand when I'm
sentences.zh: 它们用它来驱赶讨厌的东西，不是真正的大型捕食者，而是讨厌的东西，当然也包括我那只

sentences.en: feeling around their home and trying to figure out what they've had for lunch yesterday.
sentences.zh: 在它们家里摸索，试图弄清楚它们昨天午餐吃了什么的手。

sentences.en: So, one of my favorite anecdotes, I really have to tell you this one.
sentences.zh: 所以，我最喜欢的轶事之一，我真的得告诉你这个。

sentences.en: They have the giant Pacific octopus pretty well all the time at the Seattle Aquarium.
sentences.zh: 西雅图水族馆几乎一直都有大太平洋章鱼。

sentences.en: And these animals are active at night, and they prefer that it's dark at night.
sentences.zh: 这些动物在夜间活动，而且它们更喜欢夜间黑暗的环境。

sentences.en: And there was one situation where they had the nightlight on over top of the octopus tank.
sentences.zh: 有一次，它们在章鱼缸上方开了夜灯。

sentences.en: And the octopus simply reached up with its siphon, jetted a jet of water at the light and shorted it up.
sentences.zh: 那只章鱼直接用虹吸管对准灯喷了一股水，导致灯短路了。

sentences.en: What the heck?
sentences.zh: 搞什么鬼？

sentences.en: You have to wonder how it figured out that it could do that.
sentences.zh: 你不得不佩服它是怎么想出能这么做的。

sentences.en: My guess is that they would have a general habit of jetting water at nuisances, like pesky researchers and scavenging fish.
sentences.zh: 我的猜测是，它们有一种向讨厌的东西喷水的习惯，比如烦人的研究人员和食腐鱼类。

sentences.en: And there are reports of octopuses in labs that have done things like squirted at researchers that maybe they didn't like for some reason.
sentences.zh: 有报道称，实验室里的章鱼曾做过一些事情，比如向它们出于某种原因可能不喜欢的科研人员喷水。

sentences.en: I mean, it was always the same person, right, when this one octopus was doing that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当这只章鱼这样做的时候，总是针对同一个人，对吧。

sentences.en: Let me ask you, are we anthropomorphizing them, or do they have distinct personalities?
sentences.zh: 请问，我们是在拟人化它们，还是它们确实有独特的个性？

sentences.en: Well, there's two questions there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有两个问题。

sentences.en: The first question is, can they tell individual humans apart?
sentences.zh: 第一个问题是，它们能区分不同的人类个体吗？

sentences.en: And with my colleague Roland Anderson at the Seattle Aquarium, we did conduct tests to see whether they could recognize individual humans.
sentences.zh: 我和西雅图水族馆的同事罗兰·安德森一起进行了测试，看看它们是否能识别不同的人类。

sentences.en: And the answer was, yes, they can.
sentences.zh: 答案是，是的，它们可以。

sentences.en: And by the way, the two subjects, one of whom, of course, was Roland, dressed in the same Seattle
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这两个受试者，其中一个当然是罗兰，穿着同样的西雅图

sentences.en: Aquarium t-shirt.
sentences.zh: 水族馆T恤。

sentences.en: So that clue wasn't available to them.
sentences.zh: 所以它们无法利用那个线索。

sentences.en: And we didn't actually figure out what clues were available, though they were different shapes and sizes.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上并没有弄清楚它们利用了什么线索，尽管他们体型和形状不同。

sentences.en: Still, that's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 不过，这已经很厉害了。

sentences.en: They can tell us apart.
sentences.zh: 它们能把我们区分开。

sentences.en: Now, you've written that octopuses are tremendous explorers and that they really have an insatiable desire for moving around.
sentences.zh: 您写过章鱼是伟大的探险家，它们确实有一种永不满足的四处走动的欲望。

sentences.en: I mean, they just don't stay in one place.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们就是不会待在一个地方。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: What does that look like in the wild or even in an aquarium?
sentences.zh: 在野外甚至在水族馆里，这看起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: What happens to an octopus that is an explorer and is confined?
sentences.zh: 一只喜欢探索却被关起来的章鱼会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, I'm really jealous, actually, of the octopus arms, because they've got eight of them, and they can explore separately with every one of them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实我真的很嫉妒章鱼的触手，因为它们有八条，而且每一条都可以独立探索。

sentences.en: So actually, when they're hunting, they're not actually hunting by vision.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，当它们捕猎时，并不是靠视觉。

sentences.en: They go to likely places, and then they stick their arms in crevices and snake them along cracks and explore the algae by sort of fueling up the stems and down the leaves.
sentences.zh: 它们会去可能的地方，然后把触手伸进缝隙，沿着裂缝蜿蜒而行，通过沿着茎向上和向下沿着叶子探索藻类。

sentences.en: And so all the time, they're picking up information through their suckers.
sentences.zh: 所以它们一直在通过吸盘获取信息。

sentences.en: By the way, each sucker has hundreds of chemical anti-tactile receptors, and each arm has hundreds of suckers.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，每个吸盘都有数百个化学和触觉感受器，每条触手都有数百个吸盘。

sentences.en: So they've got tons and tons and tons of information.
sentences.zh: 所以它们拥有海量的信息。

sentences.en: Speaking of information and how octopuses gather it, I mean, they're clearly using their arms for a lot of this work, but they do have brains.
sentences.zh: 说到信息以及章鱼如何收集信息，它们显然在用触手完成很多工作，但它们确实有大脑。

sentences.en: In fact, I understand they have more than one brain.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我听说它们不止一个大脑。

sentences.en: I mean, how is the octopus brain organized?
sentences.zh: 章鱼的大脑是如何组织的？

sentences.en: No, no, it's a popular fallacy.
sentences.zh: 不，不，那是一个流行的谬论。

sentences.en: They have one central brain.
sentences.zh: 它们只有一个中央大脑。

sentences.en: But what this comes from is the fact that only two-fifths of the nerves of the octopus are in the brain.
sentences.zh: 但这种说法源于这样一个事实：章鱼只有五分之二的神经在大脑中。

sentences.en: Three-fifths are out there in the arMs. And each arm, in fact, has a chain of ganglia down its dorsal surface.
sentences.zh: 五分之三在触手里。事实上，每条触手的背侧都有一串神经节。

sentences.en: Each one of these ganglia is actually centered over one of the suckers.
sentences.zh: 这些神经节中的每一个实际上都位于一个吸盘上方。

sentences.en: And though there's a sucker ganglion, this chain of ganglia is really responsible for making sure the suckers do what
sentences.zh: 虽然有一个吸盘神经节，但这串神经节确实负责确保吸盘做它们

sentences.en: they're supposed to do and feel and smell what they're supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 该做的事，并感知和嗅出它们该感知和嗅出的东西。

sentences.en: But they're not a brain.
sentences.zh: 但它们不是大脑。

sentences.en: One thing to call them is a plexus.
sentences.zh: 可以称它们为神经丛。

sentences.en: And a plexus is a series of same units, which does have some organization, but it doesn't have a central controller.
sentences.zh: 神经丛是一系列相同的单元，确实有一些组织，但没有中央控制器。

sentences.en: Another way to look at it is what's going on in the arms is subroutines.
sentences.zh: 另一种看待方式是触手中发生的是子程序。

sentences.en: So the octopus brain doesn't tell the arms what to do in detail.
sentences.zh: 所以章鱼的大脑不会详细告诉触手该做什么。

sentences.en: Somebody described it as the octopus brain tells the ganglia what to tell the arms to do.
sentences.zh: 有人形容说，章鱼大脑告诉神经节该让触手做什么。

sentences.en: There's an evolutionary reason for this, and I have to back up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 这背后有进化原因，我得稍微回顾一下。

sentences.en: Octopuses have no bones.
sentences.zh: 章鱼没有骨头。

sentences.en: And when you think about it, if you had no bones, how could you possibly move whole things, move parts of you around?
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，如果你没有骨头，怎么可能移动整个身体，移动身体的各个部分呢？

sentences.en: And the answer to that is specifically in the arms, that the octopus stiffens some of the muscles to act as temporary skeletons.
sentences.zh: 答案就在触手中，章鱼会收紧一些肌肉作为临时骨架。

sentences.en: And then the other muscles articulate against those temporary skeletons.
sentences.zh: 然后其他肌肉在这些临时骨架上进行关节运动。

sentences.en: It's really way more flexibility than we have.
sentences.zh: 这确实比我们拥有的灵活性要高得多。

sentences.en: But if you think about it, you couldn't possibly program all that in the brain.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想一想，你不可能在大脑中编程所有这些动作。

sentences.en: So what the brain does is it sends out general signals to the ganglia and the ganglia go, oh, okay, I'm supposed to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以大脑所做的是向神经节发送一般信号，神经节就会说，哦，好的，我该做这个了。

sentences.en: So it's true that the arms have a lot of autonomy.
sentences.zh: 所以触手确实有很大的自主权，这是真的。

sentences.en: There are long-armed octopuses that actually have autonomy that they can cast off an arm if they're threatened.
sentences.zh: 有些长臂章鱼确实有自主权，如果受到威胁，它们可以断掉一条触手。

sentences.en: And one of these cast off arms will actually crawl down your hand and the suckers will make contact with whatever is underneath them.
sentences.zh: 而其中一条断掉的触手实际上会爬过你的手，吸盘会与它们下方的任何东西接触。

sentences.en: There's a rumor, I've never seen this, but anyway, first of all, I should say that if an item out there in the environment is not terribly interesting and small.
sentences.zh: 有个传闻，我从来没见过，但不管怎样，首先我应该说，如果环境中的某个东西不是特别有趣且很小。

sentences.en: The octopus may reach out an arm, hold onto it with the suckers at the tip, and passes sucker
sentences.zh: 章鱼可能会伸出一只触手，用尖端的吸盘抓住它，然后一个吸盘

sentences.en: by sucker by sucker by sucker up to the mouth to decide whether it's useful and good to taste.
sentences.zh: 接一个吸盘地把它传送到嘴边，以决定它是否有用，味道好不好。

sentences.en: And I've done an ethogram, which is a description of all the behaviors of the octopuses.
sentences.zh: 我做过一个行为谱，也就是对章鱼所有行为的描述。

sentences.en: And in this particular case, I call this action conveyor belt.
sentences.zh: 在这种特殊情况下，我把这个动作称为“传送带”。

sentences.en: But the rumor is, and I haven't seen this, but the rumor is that an arm that has been cast off from the body can pick up a sucker and pass it from sucker
sentences.zh: 但传闻是——我没见过——传闻说，一条从身体上断掉的触手可以捡起一个吸盘，并把它从一个吸盘

sentences.en: to sucker to sucker towards the month that isn't there anymore.
sentences.zh: 传向另一个吸盘，传向那个已经不存在的嘴。

sentences.en: So that's a lot of organization, but it's not a brain because it's not a decision maker.
sentences.zh: 所以这有很多组织性，但它不是大脑，因为它不是决策者。

sentences.en: And for me, subroutines is the best way to think about it.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，把它们看作子程序是最好的方式。

sentences.en: This isn't exactly a psychological question, but since you know so much about cephalopods, and I don't, how do octopuses camouflage themselves so well?
sentences.zh: 这不完全是一个心理学问题，但既然您对头足类动物了解这么多，而我了解不多，章鱼是如何如此完美地伪装自己的？

sentences.en: My understanding is that they have very limited color vision.
sentences.zh: 我的理解是它们有非常有限的色觉。

sentences.en: So what does it work when they do this?
sentences.zh: 那么它们做这件事时是怎么起作用的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's terribly ironic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这太讽刺了。

sentences.en: They do not have color vision, and yet they can use color in camouflage.
sentences.zh: 它们没有色觉，却能在伪装中使用颜色。

sentences.en: And exactly how they do it, we do not know.
sentences.zh: 至于它们究竟是如何做到的，我们不得而知。

sentences.en: It's one of the big paradoxes of octopus behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是章鱼行为的一大悖论。

sentences.en: But they have fabulous camouflage.
sentences.zh: 但它们有极好的伪装。

sentences.en: And the reason they have such good camouflage, they have many organs in the skin, chromatophores.
sentences.zh: 它们之所以有这么好的伪装，是因为它们的皮肤里有很多器官，叫色素细胞。

sentences.en: Each of those chromatophores is an elastic sac
sentences.zh: 每一个色素细胞都是一个弹性囊，

sentences.en: containing pigments that are either yellow or red or brown black.
sentences.zh: 里面含有黄色、红色或棕黑色的色素。

sentences.en: And each of those elastic sacs has muscles pulling it out.
sentences.zh: 每一个弹性囊都有肌肉将其拉开。

sentences.en: So when the muscles relax, you can't see anything.
sentences.zh: 所以当肌肉放松时，你什么也看不见。

sentences.en: You can see the reflective surfaces below.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到下面的反射表面。

sentences.en: When they pull it out, suddenly you see the color.
sentences.zh: 当它们拉开时，你突然就看到了颜色。

sentences.en: And the reason they're so good at this is, given that it's muscles, they could be very specific.
sentences.zh: 它们之所以如此擅长这一点，是因为既然是肌肉控制，它们就可以非常精确。

sentences.en: So there's really more control to an area of at least a millimeter square, probably smaller.
sentences.zh: 所以对于至少一平方毫米的区域，甚至可能更小的区域，确实有更多的控制。

sentences.en: And they're very faSt. So they can change color in about 33 milliseconds.
sentences.zh: 而且它们非常快。所以它们可以在大约33毫秒内改变颜色。

sentences.en: And with that kind of combination, you could do anything you like.
sentences.zh: 有了这种组合，你可以做任何你想做的事。

sentences.en: Now, there are some great videos out there that show octopuses doing what looks like playing, whether they're batting a fish or doing the equivalent of bouncing a ball.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一些很棒的视频展示了章鱼做看起来像是在玩耍的行为，无论是拍打鱼还是做相当于拍球的动作。

sentences.en: Is that what they're doing?
sentences.zh: 那是他们正在做的事吗？

sentences.en: Is it your belief that they're actually playing?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们真的在玩耍吗？

sentences.en: Well, it was actually one of my research projects, the game with Roland Anderson, because we figured if any invertebrate plays, it would be the octopuses.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其实是我的研究项目之一，就是和罗兰·安德森（Roland Anderson）一起做的游戏研究，因为我们认为如果有什么无脊椎动物会玩耍，那一定是章鱼。

sentences.en: And I have a colleague, Sergio Pellas, who is a specialist at mammalian play.
sentences.zh: 我有一位同事，塞尔吉奥·佩拉斯（Sergio Pellas），他是哺乳动物玩耍行为的专家。

sentences.en: He's written a couple of books on play.
sentences.zh: 他写过几本关于玩耍的书。

sentences.en: And I remember asking him one day whether he thought that octopuses would play.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一天问他，他是否认为章鱼会玩耍。

sentences.en: And he said, well, given what you told me about them, maybe.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，根据你告诉我的关于它们的情况，也许会。

sentences.en: So Roland and I set up a situation and we figured for them to play, they'd have to be bored and safe and have something that was worth manipulating.
sentences.zh: 于是罗兰和我设计了一个情境，我们认为要让它们玩耍，它们必须感到无聊、安全，并且有值得摆弄的东西。

sentences.en: This is one of my favorite studies of all times, by the way, for a very interesting reason.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这是我最喜欢的各项研究之一，原因非常有趣。

sentences.en: So we set up a situation where we had octopuses in the lab at the aquarium.
sentences.zh: 我们在水族馆的实验室里为章鱼设置了一个环境。

sentences.en: There was nothing in the lab except a place to hide and a floating pill bottle, which was, I guess it had about one quarter full of water.
sentences.zh: 实验室里除了一个藏身之处和一个漂浮的药瓶外什么都没有，我想那瓶子里大概装了四分之一的水。

sentences.en: So it floated gently on the surface.
sentences.zh: 所以它轻轻地漂浮在水面上。

sentences.en: And the first reaction of all the six octopuses we used was to just grab it, pull it into the mouth, feel around with the suckers and figure out that it wasn't
sentences.zh: 我们所用的六只章鱼的第一反应都是直接抓住它，把它拉进嘴里，用吸盘摸索一番，然后发现它

sentences.en: worth anything in terms of food and let it go.
sentences.zh: 作为食物毫无价值，于是就把它放开了。

sentences.en: Two of the six by about the fourth child used them.
sentences.zh: 六只中有两只在大约第四次尝试时开始使用它。

sentences.en: And this was actually serendipity, because we had the octopus at one end of the aquarium and the water intake from circulation at the other end.
sentences.zh: 这其实是偶然发现的，因为我们将章鱼放在水族馆的一端，而循环系统的进水口在另一端。

sentences.en: So two of the octopuses aimed a water jet and sent the pill bottle down to the intake where it came floating back to them.
sentences.zh: 于是两只章鱼瞄准药瓶喷水，把瓶子推向进水口，然后瓶子又漂回了它们身边。

sentences.en: Now, if you do it once, you're not going to call that play.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你只做一次，你不会称之为玩耍。

sentences.en: I think one of them it was 16 times and one of them it was 10 times.
sentences.zh: 我想其中一只做了16次，另一只做了10次。

sentences.en: And that's play.
sentences.zh: 那就是玩耍。

sentences.en: Having contacts with the world of animal play has been some time talking to Sergio and also to
sentences.zh: 与动物玩耍世界建立联系，得益于我与塞尔吉奥以及

sentences.en: Gordon Burghardt, who has gave a book on play.
sentences.zh: 戈登·伯格哈特（Gordon Burghardt）的交流，他写过一本关于玩耍的书。

sentences.en: And Gordon discusses this situation and says it passes all the rules for play.
sentences.zh: 戈登讨论了这种情况，并表示它符合玩耍的所有准则。

sentences.en: And the animals are doing this alone, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这些动物是独自做这件事的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you can't put two octopuses in the same tank.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不能把两只章鱼放在同一个水箱里。

sentences.en: Well, it depends on the species, but yes, there are some species where if you put two octopuses in the same tank, you'll end up with one welfare octopus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于物种，但确实，有些物种如果你把两只章鱼放在同一个水箱里，最后只会剩下一只健康的章鱼。

sentences.en: And that's a characteristic of the whole group, which means you really can never count on them being truly social, because they are all potentially at least cannibalistic.
sentences.zh: 这是整个群体的特征，这意味着你真的不能指望它们是真正社交性的，因为它们至少都有潜在的同类相食倾向。

sentences.en: And that's why you're not going to see octopuses doing social play, because they don't like each other enough.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你不会看到章鱼进行社交性玩耍，因为它们彼此之间不够喜欢。

sentences.en: You also teach a course in human-animal interaction.
sentences.zh: 你还教授一门关于人与动物互动的课程。

sentences.en: How did you get interested in that topic?
sentences.zh: 你是如何对这个话题产生兴趣的？

sentences.en: And how does it tie in with your research on cephalopods?
sentences.zh: 它与你对头足类动物的研究有什么联系？

sentences.en: Well, I'm in a psychology department and I teach psychology courses.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在心理学系，我教授心理学课程。

sentences.en: So, of course, I have one foot in the psychology kingdom.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，我的一只脚踏在心理学的领域里。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, I have a master's in biology.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，我拥有生物学硕士学位。

sentences.en: And clearly, a lot of understanding of biology is a general sweep.
sentences.zh: 显然，对生物学的很多理解是一个宏观的概览。

sentences.en: So, in some ways, I found myself at the boundary.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某些方面，我发现自己处于边界上。

sentences.en: And one of the courses I taught for, I think, 25, 30 years was human perception.
sentences.zh: 我教授了大约25到30年的一门课程是人类感知。

sentences.en: And I found it particularly useful to be able to teach human perception while
sentences.zh: 我发现，在教授人类感知的同时，

sentences.en: having a knowledge of what I would call the sweep in the scope of perception across the animal kingdom,
sentences.zh: 掌握我所说的整个动物界的感知范围是非常有用的，

sentences.en: because I didn't just see our sensory input as something that was special and different, and only for us.
sentences.zh: 因为我并不认为我们的感官输入是某种特殊且不同的、仅属于我们的东西。

sentences.en: I could compare it with other animal sensations.
sentences.zh: 我可以把它与其他动物的感官进行比较。

sentences.en: So, I remember how it started, actually, because I have been working on animal welfare, because the invertebrates in general are not protected in research.
sentences.zh: 所以，我记得它是怎么开始的，实际上，因为我一直致力于动物福利，因为无脊椎动物在研究中通常不受保护。

sentences.en: Even in the United States right now, they're not yet protected.
sentences.zh: 即使在美国，现在它们也还没有受到保护。

sentences.en: And we had a department member who became ill, and the department chair came to me and said, do you think you can teach anything in animal behavior?
sentences.zh: 我们系里有一位成员生病了，系主任来找我，问我是否认为自己能教动物行为学方面的课程？

sentences.en: Some kind of seminar that has something to do with the welfare stuff.
sentences.zh: 某种与福利相关的研讨会。

sentences.en: And I thought, oh, sure.
sentences.zh: 我想，哦，当然可以。

sentences.en: Because if you think about it, we're in a world full of animals, and yet we don't really think about the interactions with them.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你仔细想想，我们生活在一个充满动物的世界里，但我们并没有真正思考过与它们的互动。

sentences.en: And they're very, very important, because we are now, as people keep saying, in the anthropocene.
sentences.zh: 它们非常、非常重要，因为正如人们一直所说，我们现在处于人类世。

sentences.en: Everything that we do is affecting every animal.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的一切都在影响着每一只动物。

sentences.en: So, I designed a course that would help get at that.
sentences.zh: 所以我设计了一门课程来帮助解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And my students enjoy it very much, actually, because it kind of opens our eyes to things that they haven't thought about that they are doing and seeing.
sentences.zh: 我的学生们实际上非常喜欢它，因为它让我们睁开眼睛，看到了他们以前从未想过自己正在做和正在看的事情。

sentences.en: But one of the things I had them do to begin with is talk about their individual philosophy with regards to animals.
sentences.zh: 但我让他们做的第一件事就是谈谈他们个人关于动物的哲学观。

sentences.en: And to begin with, I used the Western philosophers.
sentences.zh: 起初，我使用了西方哲学家的观点。

sentences.en: And then I thought, wait a minute, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，等等，等等。

sentences.en: We're not the only philosophy game in town.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是唯一的哲学流派。

sentences.en: So, I got a Plains
sentences.zh: 所以我引入了平原印第安人的哲学，

sentences.en: Indian philosophy, and I got Buddhist philosophy.
sentences.zh: 还有佛教哲学。

sentences.en: And then I said to the students, okay, here's some examples.
sentences.zh: 然后我对学生们说，好吧，这里有一些例子。

sentences.en: Each of you should think about what yours is.
sentences.zh: 你们每个人都应该思考一下自己的哲学观是什么。

sentences.en: But then I went over the different situations in which we do interact with animals.
sentences.zh: 但随后我回顾了我们与动物互动的不同情况。

sentences.en: And I said, okay, we're going to start at the closest possible.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我们从最亲近的开始。

sentences.en: And every year, I see my students saying, oh, dogs and cats.
sentences.zh: 每年，我都会看到学生们说，哦，猫和狗。

sentences.en: And I said, parasites.
sentences.zh: 我说，寄生虫。

sentences.en: Think of leeches.
sentences.zh: 想想水蛭。

sentences.en: Think of nets.
sentences.zh: 想想蚊子。

sentences.en: And lately, I've detoured to telling them about the human microbiome, which is very important in our psychological and physiological functioning.
sentences.zh: 最近，我转而向他们讲述人类微生物组，这在我们的心理和生理功能中非常重要。

sentences.en: And yet we're only learning about it.
sentences.zh: 然而我们才刚刚开始了解它。

sentences.en: It's amazing to think about.
sentences.zh: 想到这一点真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: A huge proportion of us is not us.
sentences.zh: 我们身体的很大一部分并不是我们自己。

sentences.en: Or as I said to my students, you know, you see me walking across the classroom floor.
sentences.zh: 或者正如我对学生们所说，你知道，你看到我走过教室的地板。

sentences.en: But actually, I'm a community.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我是一个群落。

sentences.en: I want to go back to something you said a minute ago about how octopuses are not protected in research.
sentences.zh: 我想回到你刚才说的一点，关于章鱼在研究中不受保护的问题。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: How are they not protected?
sentences.zh: 它们怎么不受保护？

sentences.en: How should they be protected?
sentences.zh: 它们应该如何受到保护？

sentences.en: It is about to change.
sentences.zh: 这即将改变。

sentences.en: But presently, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但目前，美国

sentences.en: Department of Agriculture rules say that you could do anything to an invertebrate that you could do to a dissected out piece of tissue,
sentences.zh: 农业部的规定说，你可以对无脊椎动物做任何你可以对解剖出来的组织碎片做的事情，

sentences.en: which is pretty horrible if you think of an octopus.
sentences.zh: 如果你想到章鱼，这真是太可怕了。

sentences.en: Way back in the 1990s, I had a colleague who was on the Canadian Council of Animal Care.
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪90年代，我有一位同事是加拿大动物护理委员会的成员。

sentences.en: And she came down the hallway to me one day and said, do you think of your octopus as a tissue?
sentences.zh: 有一天她走过走廊对我说，你把你的章鱼看作组织吗？

sentences.en: And I said, no, of course not.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，当然不是。

sentences.en: But because she was a member of the CCAC, she set up a mini committee.
sentences.zh: 但因为她是加拿大动物护理委员会（CCAC）的成员，她成立了一个小型委员会。

sentences.en: And in Canada, we were the first to say some invertebrates, specifically cephalopods, are protected in research the same as vertebrates.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大，我们是第一个提出某些无脊椎动物，特别是头足类动物，在研究中应受到与脊椎动物相同保护的国家。

sentences.en: When the European Union organized, they thought about this and discussed this and consulted with people like me who knew about
sentences.zh: 当欧盟组织起来时，他们考虑并讨论了这个问题，并咨询了像我这样了解

sentences.en: these things and decided that this should be true in the EU.
sentences.zh: 这些事情的人，并决定这在欧盟也应该适用。

sentences.en: When the UK broke off from the EU and Brexit, they had a hand for quite a while, a group called Crustacean Compassion.
sentences.zh: 当英国脱欧时，他们有一段时间有一个名为“甲壳类动物同情”（Crustacean Compassion）的组织。

sentences.en: And these people said, hey, we need to protect cephalopods, but we need to protect decopod crustaceans, shrimp, lobsters, crabs.
sentences.zh: 这些人说，嘿，我们需要保护头足类动物，但我们也需要保护十足目甲壳类动物，比如虾、龙虾、螃蟹。

sentences.en: And they did actually, they got a consultant, Jonathan Birch, from the London School of Economics.
sentences.zh: 他们确实做到了，他们聘请了伦敦政治经济学院的顾问乔纳森·伯奇（Jonathan Birch）。

sentences.en: And he wrote a, you know, a major report, sent it to the House of Commons and the House of Commons said, okay, so they're protected.
sentences.zh: 他写了一份重要的报告，提交给了下议院，下议院说，好吧，它们受到保护了。

sentences.en: In the United States, there is a group called Physicians for Social Responsibility in Harvard.
sentences.zh: 在美国，有一个名为“医生社会责任组织”（Physicians for Social Responsibility）的哈佛团体。

sentences.en: And they had been agitating for quite a while, specifically to the NIH, National Institute of Health, to institute some protection for cephalopods.
sentences.zh: 他们已经游说了一段时间，专门向美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）申请为头足类动物制定一些保护措施。

sentences.en: Now, I guess it was about a year and a half ago,
sentences.zh: 现在，我想大约是一年半前，

sentences.en: they weren't getting anywhere with NIH, so they decided that they would hold a congressional briefing.
sentences.zh: 他们在NIH那里没有取得任何进展，所以他们决定举行一次国会简报会。

sentences.en: And they had met some members of Congress and members of the Senate, send somebody to listen to the information.
sentences.zh: 他们会见了一些国会议员和参议员，派人去听取这些信息。

sentences.en: And I had the pleasure of making part in a congressional briefing, which is something I could never imagine that I would have done in my life, by Zoom.
sentences.zh: 我有幸通过Zoom参加了国会简报会，这是我一生中从未想象过会做的事情。

sentences.en: But still,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，

sentences.en: initially, the NIH said, oh, well, we don't really know, we don't need to do this.
sentences.zh: 最初，NIH说，哦，好吧，我们不太清楚，我们不需要这样做。

sentences.en: But they said, about three or four months ago, they decided that it probably would be useful to have some guidelines.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，大约三四个月前，他们决定制定一些指导方针可能是有用的。

sentences.en: And they sent out to everyone their provisional guidelines.
sentences.zh: 他们向所有人发送了临时指导方针。

sentences.en: And the Physicians for
sentences.zh: 而“医生社会责任组织”

sentences.en: Social Responsibility looked at it and said, no, no, it's not good enough because you just say it's suggested.
sentences.zh: 看了之后说，不，不，这还不够好，因为你们只是说这是建议。

sentences.en: It should be actually a rule.
sentences.zh: 这实际上应该是一条规则。

sentences.en: And we're waiting to see what happens.
sentences.zh: 我们正在等待结果。

sentences.en: I think in the end, it will be required that cephalopods would be protected.
sentences.zh: 我认为最终，头足类动物受到保护将成为强制性要求。

sentences.en: I should say, by the way, that I've done research with colleagues in University of Southern California, in New York.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我应该说，我曾与南加州大学和纽约的同事一起进行过研究。

sentences.en: And most of the people who care about animal welfare in universities treat the cephalopods as honorary vertebrates.
sentences.zh: 大多数在大学里关心动物福利的人都把头足类动物视为名誉脊椎动物。

sentences.en: But we have a long way to go.
sentences.zh: 但我们还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: There's still most of the countries in the world that don't protect these animals.
sentences.zh: 世界上大多数国家仍然不保护这些动物。

sentences.en: So just I'm wondering, as a psychologist, how you got so interested in cephalopods and octopuses in particular?
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇，作为一名心理学家，你是如何对头足类动物，特别是章鱼产生如此浓厚兴趣的？

sentences.en: Well, it was actually the other way around.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: I grew up beside the ocean.
sentences.zh: 我在海边长大。

sentences.en: And I got fascinated with intertidal animals.
sentences.zh: 我对潮间带动物着迷。

sentences.en: And I thought, okay,
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，

sentences.en: I'm going to study sea animals.
sentences.zh: 我要研究海洋动物。

sentences.en: And so I did my bachelor's and master's in biology departments.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在生物系完成了我的学士和硕士学位。

sentences.en: And my professor, when I was a billionaire kind of Florida State University, he said, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我在佛罗里达州立大学时，我的教授说，你知道，

sentences.en: you should really go do your PhD with somebody who was working with octopus behavior.
sentences.zh: 你真的应该去跟一位研究章鱼行为的人攻读博士学位。

sentences.en: And there weren't very many people doing octopus behavior.
sentences.zh: 当时研究章鱼行为的人并不多。

sentences.en: There still aren't.
sentences.zh: 现在依然不多。

sentences.en: Okay, there should be more.
sentences.zh: 好吧，应该更多才对。

sentences.en: But I went to work with a professor who was in the psychology department.
sentences.zh: 但我去了一位在心理学系的教授那里工作。

sentences.en: And he was what we sometimes call in the business a toxic professor.
sentences.zh: 他就是我们行内有时所说的“有毒教授”。

sentences.en: And when he realized I was good, he didn't want to work with me anymore.
sentences.zh: 当他意识到我很优秀时，他就不想再和我一起工作了。

sentences.en: So I finished my PhD with another professor working with human sensory motor coordination.
sentences.zh: 所以我换了另一位教授完成了我的博士学位，研究人类感觉运动协调。

sentences.en: And gradually, I drifted back to purely cephalopods.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，我又回到了纯粹的头足类动物研究上。

sentences.en: But I've got, as I said, one foot in each camp.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，我两边都占着。

sentences.en: Now, I mentioned in my introduction that you were an advisor to the
sentences.zh: 现在，我在介绍中提到你是Netflix纪录片《我的章鱼老师》的顾问。

sentences.en: Netflix documentary, My Octopus Teacher.
sentences.zh: 这是怎么促成的？

sentences.en: How did that come about?
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些看过的人来说，它在反映和捕捉你在研究中看到的章鱼行为范围方面做得好吗？

sentences.en: And just as a follow-up for those of us who have seen it, did it do a good job of reflecting and capturing the range of octopus behavior that you've seen in your research?
sentences.zh: 嗯，《我的章鱼老师》的制片人克雷格·福斯特（Craig Foster），

sentences.en: Well, Craig Foster, who's the producer of My Octopus Teacher,
sentences.zh: 之前曾向BBC的《蓝色星球》系列发送过一些素材。

sentences.en: had previously sent some footage to the BBC Blue Planet series.
sentences.zh: BBC的《蓝色星球》系列对确保生物学准确性非常、非常挑剔。

sentences.en: And the BBC Blue Planet series are very, very picky about making sure the biology is correct.
sentences.zh: 我因为这一点而爱他们。

sentences.en: I love them for that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们联系了我，说，嘿，我们想知道我们得到的这些素材是否准确。

sentences.en: So they got in touch with me and said, hey, we want to know if this footage that we've got is accurate.
sentences.zh: 你能看一看吗？

sentences.en: Would you take a look at it?
sentences.zh: 我说，当然。

sentences.en: I said, sure.
sentences.zh: 我和他们一起工作了一段时间。

sentences.en: I'll work with them for a while.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间结束时，制片人说，顺便说一下，电影制作人想和你谈谈。

sentences.en: And at the end of that time, the producer said, by the way, the filmmaker would kind of like to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，如果我们把你的邮箱给他，没问题。

sentences.en: I said, okay, if we give him your email, sure, no problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是我发现他在制作这部电影的过程。

sentences.en: And so that's how I found out that he was doing the film.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，他想和BBC的人一样挑剔，确保行为是正确的。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, he wanted to be as picky about making sure the behavior was correct as the BBC people were.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说再次没问题。

sentences.en: And that, once again, was fine with me.
sentences.zh: 所以他们飞我到南非待了10天，这样我们就可以查看电影素材，看看它是否准确。

sentences.en: So they flew me to South Africa for 10 days so we could look over film footage and see that it was accurate.
sentences.zh: 他在某些方面和我一样，他实际上是一位博物学家。我的意思是，他是一位非常出色的电影制作人，但他对自然世界非常、非常感兴趣，

sentences.en: And he's, in some ways, the way I am, he's actually a naturaliSt. I mean, he's a very good filmmaker, but he's very, very interested in the natural world,
sentences.zh: 属于一个致力于拯救海洋的组织，并且对海带森林特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: belongs to an organization that's working on saving the oceans and is particularly interested in the kelp forests.
sentences.zh: 所以和他一起工作很有趣。

sentences.en: So he was fun to work with.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我去年休了六个月的学术假，我回到了南非并拜访了他，最后还指导了一名开普敦大学的学生。

sentences.en: And in fact, I had my sabbatical last year for six months, and I went back to South Africa and visited with him, and also ended up directing a student in University of Cape Town.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次非常、非常愉快的合作。

sentences.en: So it was a very, very nice association.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次非常、非常愉快的合作。

sentences.en: He is doing something that I think is quite surprising.
sentences.zh: 他正在做的事情，我觉得相当令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And I'm very jealous, by the way, he lives just up the hill from his smuggling site where he goes swimming every day.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我非常嫉妒他，他住的地方离他每天游泳的那个走私地点只有上坡路之遥。

sentences.en: And he's decided he wants to find 1,000 animal species in this kelp foreSt. Oh, I should say, by the way, that by his sort of doggone watching
sentences.zh: 他决定要在这一片海带森林里找到1000种动物。哦，顺便说一下，我应该说，通过他那种极其专注的观察，

sentences.en: what's going on, he has already discovered a few species that are new to science.
sentences.zh: 他已经发现了一些科学界尚未记录的新物种。

sentences.en: Wow, that's great.
sentences.zh: 哇，那太棒了。

sentences.en: And he works with a scientist at the University of Cape Town.
sentences.zh: 而且他与开普敦大学的一位科学家有合作。

sentences.en: Actually, this particular individual
sentences.zh: 事实上，这位特别的人，

sentences.en: has 100 new species to his name.
sentences.zh: 已经有100个新物种以他的名字命名了。

sentences.en: But I think Craig has discovered about four or five of them.
sentences.zh: 但我认为克雷格（Craig）自己大约发现了其中的四五个。

sentences.en: So it's a wonderful association.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常美妙的合作。

sentences.en: Not too shabby.
sentences.zh: 相当不错。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 那太神奇了。

sentences.en: We should do an awful lot more of that.
sentences.zh: 我们应该多做一些这样的事情。

sentences.en: Actually, citizen science is something that I firmly believe in.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我坚定地相信公民科学。

sentences.en: It belongs to them.
sentences.zh: 它属于他们。

sentences.en: It belongs to the people.
sentences.zh: 它属于大众。

sentences.en: Science is funded by the people, supported by those people.
sentences.zh: 科学是由大众资助的，由大众支持的。

sentences.en: They have every right to know.
sentences.zh: 他们完全有权知道。

sentences.en: And besides, it's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 而且，这非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: They should know.
sentences.zh: 他们应该知道。

sentences.en: So I'm always happy to talk to anybody about saflopods.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是很乐意和任何人谈论头足类动物。

sentences.en: How is the study of octopuses translating into the study and the understanding of other animals?
sentences.zh: 对章鱼的研究是如何转化为对其他动物的研究和理解的？

sentences.en: The simplest first step is to say that we always presumed that mammals, particularly primates, particularly homo sapiens, kind of had the corner on intelligence.
sentences.zh: 最简单的第一步是说，我们一直认为哺乳动物，特别是灵长类动物，特别是智人，在智力方面占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: And so the only model we have for evolution of intelligence was the higher mammals.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有的唯一关于智力进化的模型就是高等哺乳动物。

sentences.en: But then you turn around and you say, wait a minute, there's another model.
sentences.zh: 但当你回过头来说，等一下，还有另一个模型。

sentences.en: And when you say there's another model, you stop thinking that you know the way it happens.
sentences.zh: 当你提出有另一个模型时，你就不会再认为自己了解事情发生的方式了。

sentences.en: When you say there's two ways that you can talk about the evolution of intelligence, then you say, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 当你意识到有两种方式可以谈论智力的进化时，你就会说，哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: Maybe artificial intelligence could use some different way.
sentences.zh: 也许人工智能可以采用不同的方式。

sentences.en: Maybe other animal species are evolving towards intelligence in a whole different group.
sentences.zh: 也许其他动物物种正在向一个完全不同的群体进化出智力。

sentences.en: Maybe there are different models.
sentences.zh: 也许存在不同的模型。

sentences.en: And one of the interesting models is the insects.
sentences.zh: 其中一个有趣的模型是昆虫。

sentences.en: Once again, totally different from us, but totally different from the saflopods.
sentences.zh: 再一次，它们与我们完全不同，但也与头足类动物完全不同。

sentences.en: And the social insects, like the honeybees are very, very interesting.
sentences.zh: 而社会性昆虫，比如蜜蜂，就非常、非常有趣。

sentences.en: And Lars Chitka has a small book about the honeybee intelligence.
sentences.zh: 拉尔斯·奇特卡（Lars Chitka）有一本关于蜜蜂智力的小书。

sentences.en: And anybody who wants to look for a third root should be looking at insects.
sentences.zh: 任何想寻找第三条根源的人都应该关注昆虫。

sentences.en: And there's another reason.
sentences.zh: 而且还有另一个原因。

sentences.en: Insects are 60% of the animals on the planet.
sentences.zh: 昆虫占地球上动物总数的60%。

sentences.en: And we have been ignoring them and killing them and demeaning them.
sentences.zh: 而我们一直忽视它们、杀害它们、贬低它们。

sentences.en: And we need to study them.
sentences.zh: 我们需要研究它们。

sentences.en: I was just last week reading a study about ants and how carpenter ants have figured out how to amputate legs of their colleagues in the colony.
sentences.zh: 我上周刚读到一项关于蚂蚁的研究，讲的是木匠蚁是如何想出办法截掉蚁群中同伴的腿的。

sentences.en: But only if the leg is injured in a certain place.
sentences.zh: 但前提是腿受伤的位置必须在特定区域。

sentences.en: If it's injured too far away from the body, there's no point in amputating.
sentences.zh: 如果受伤位置离身体太远，截肢就没有意义了。

sentences.en: But if it's close to the body, they can amputate it and the ant will continue to live.
sentences.zh: 但如果靠近身体，它们就可以截掉它，蚂蚁还能继续活下去。

sentences.en: It will survive.
sentences.zh: 它能存活下来。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So I'll give you an example of cross-group abilities.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你举一个跨群体能力的例子。

sentences.en: I used to think there are three species groups that garden.
sentences.zh: 我过去认为有三个物种群体会进行园艺。

sentences.en: One of them, of course, is homosapiens.
sentences.zh: 其中之一当然是智人。

sentences.en: One of them is the leaf-cutter ants that take pieces of leaf down into a refugium, I guess.
sentences.zh: 另一个是切叶蚁，它们把叶子碎片带到避难所，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And the fungus degrades the leaf and the ants use fungus as food.
sentences.zh: 真菌分解叶子，蚂蚁则以真菌为食。

sentences.en: But there's a third one.
sentences.zh: 但还有第三种。

sentences.en: There's a limpet.
sentences.zh: 有一种帽贝。

sentences.en: If you think of the top hatch shell that clings onto the rocks, there is a large limpet named latia, which is often called the owl limpet.
sentences.zh: 如果你想到那种吸附在岩石上的顶部壳状物，有一种大型帽贝叫Latia，通常被称为猫头鹰帽贝。

sentences.en: And it turns out that the females guard a territory, scrape algae off the rocks.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，雌性会守卫领地，刮掉岩石上的藻类。

sentences.en: But they'll go to one place, and then the next day they'll go to another place.
sentences.zh: 但它们会去一个地方，第二天又去另一个地方。

sentences.en: And in terms of their mucus trails that they make on the way, fertilize the algae.
sentences.zh: 就它们在路上留下的粘液痕迹而言，它们实际上是在为藻类施肥。

sentences.en: And they actually knock invaders off the rocks.
sentences.zh: 而且它们真的会把入侵者从岩石上撞下去。

sentences.en: And they come along like a little sort of front-end loader.
sentences.zh: 它们就像一台小型的前端装载机一样冲过来。

sentences.en: Bam!
sentences.zh: 砰！

sentences.en: And I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I'm trying to picture a limpet doing that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我正在试着想象一只帽贝那样做，是的。

sentences.en: Yes, I've never seen a picture, but someone's got to.
sentences.zh: 是的，我从未见过照片，但总有人会看到的。

sentences.en: That's pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 那真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: But it's only the females.
sentences.zh: 但只有雌性会这样做。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And they kick the males off if they don't want them for sex.
sentences.zh: 如果它们不想交配，就会把雄性踢开。

sentences.en: But I was telling an insect specialist about this at the animal behavior conference, and he said there's a kind of beetle that cultivates fungus.
sentences.zh: 我在动物行为会议上告诉一位昆虫专家这件事时，他说有一种甲虫也会培育真菌。

sentences.en: So I have to find out more about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我得去了解更多相关信息。

sentences.en: That's four.
sentences.zh: 那是第四种了。

sentences.en: It's still interesting to think about because gardens, of course, made a huge difference to our species.
sentences.zh: 思考这一点仍然很有趣，因为园艺当然对我们物种产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And we tend to think of that, I think, as one of the manifestations of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们倾向于将其视为智力的表现之一。

sentences.en: But we're not alone at doing it.
sentences.zh: 但我们并不是唯一会这样做的物种。

sentences.en: Well, clearly you have a very inquisitive mind, so I'm wondering what's next for you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然你有一个非常好奇的头脑，所以我很好奇你接下来要做什么。

sentences.en: What else are you working on these days?
sentences.zh: 这些天你还在忙些什么？

sentences.en: Well, I have a book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有一本书。

sentences.en: It's nearly finished.
sentences.zh: 快写完了。

sentences.en: And it's actually the marine ecosystems and how the marine ecosystems work.
sentences.zh: 实际上是关于海洋生态系统以及海洋生态系统是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So there's three chapters looking at the things that are critical in the marine ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 所以有三章内容是关于海洋生态系统中至关重要的事物。

sentences.en: So one of them is movement.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是运动。

sentences.en: One of them is perception.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是感知。

sentences.en: And again, this is, of course, where my background and perception comes in handy.
sentences.zh: 同样，这当然是我在感知方面的背景派上用场的地方。

sentences.en: And one of them is buoyancy.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是浮力。

sentences.en: So I'll give you an example from the buoyancy chapter, the magic number 1.025.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你举一个浮力章节的例子，神奇数字1.025。

sentences.en: What do you think that might be?
sentences.zh: 你觉得那可能是什么？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: The density of water?
sentences.zh: 水的密度？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: Did I get it?
sentences.zh: 我猜对了吗？

sentences.en: But the density of distilled water is 1.000.
sentences.zh: 但蒸馏水的密度是1.000。

sentences.en: But 1.025 is the density of salt water.
sentences.zh: 而1.025是盐水的密度。

sentences.en: Good for you.
sentences.zh: 真为你高兴。

sentences.en: I was a bio major.
sentences.zh: 我大学主修生物。

sentences.en: Ah.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: So why is that critical?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么这至关重要呢？

sentences.en: Because you float in salt water.
sentences.zh: 因为你在盐水里会浮起来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So if you float in salt water, you're fine.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在盐水里能浮起来，你就没事。

sentences.en: But if you don't, you sink.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不能，你就会下沉。

sentences.en: And the sunshine is up there.
sentences.zh: 而阳光在上面。

sentences.en: The plankton are up there.
sentences.zh: 浮游生物在上面。

sentences.en: So somehow or other, pretty well, every marine animal has to deal with, what do you do about your buoyancy?
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，几乎每一种海洋动物都必须处理这个问题：你该如何应对你的浮力？

sentences.en: Some of them have floats with air.
sentences.zh: 有些动物有充满空气的浮囊。

sentences.en: Some of them have ammonia in their tissues.
sentences.zh: 有些动物的组织里含有氨。

sentences.en: Some of them just keep moving.
sentences.zh: 有些动物只是不停地游动。

sentences.en: Tuna just keep moving.
sentences.zh: 金枪鱼就是不停地游动。

sentences.en: But life in the open ocean is about figuring out how not to sink.
sentences.zh: 但在开阔海洋中的生活，关键在于弄清楚如何不沉下去。

sentences.en: Well, I look forward to seeing your book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很期待看到你的书。

sentences.en: So keep us posted here on Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 所以请在《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology）节目上随时向我们通报进展。

sentences.en: We'll talk again.
sentences.zh: 我们还会再聊的。

sentences.en: I want to thank you very much for joining me, Dr. Mather.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您参加我的节目，马瑟博士（Dr. Mather）。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: It's been fun.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.zh: 美国心理学会。

sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
